sanskrit_verse: आस्वेव तु भुजिष्यासु दोषः स्यात् परदारवत्‌ । गम्या अपि हि नोपेयास् ताश् चेदन्यपरिग्रहाः ॥
transliteration: āsv eva tu bhujiṣyāsu doṣaḥ syāt paradāravat | gamyā api hi nopeyās tāś ced anyaparigrahāḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a woman is under the protection or guardianship of another, engaging with her constitutes the same fault as with one's neighbor's wife; even those women who are generally approachable should not be approached if they are under the custody or commitment of another.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the custodial responsibility over an individual
Causation arises through violation of protective boundaries
Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of relational integrity
Restoration logic demands re-alignment with protective dharmic structures
Consciousness alignment occurs when relational sanctity is honored
executable_legal_axioms: IF (individual A is under custodial responsibility of individual B) AND (individual C engages with A without consent or acknowledgment from B) THEN (violation of dharma has occurred)
IF (a person approaches another who is under guardianship) THEN (action is impermissible regardless of general accessibility)
IF (custody or protective status is established) THEN (general consent norms do not apply)
IF (relational boundary is violated) THEN (restorative process must engage both violator and violated)
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, the threshold of responsibility lies not in intent but in the breach of custodial integrity. The court must recognize that authority flows from the protective relationship, and any violation thereof constitutes actionable dharma-adharmic misalignment requiring immediate restoration rather than punitive consequence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that the root cause is disregard for custodial dharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals the sequential degradation of relational trust upon such transgression. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of custodial neglect enabled. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that suffering is not justice; realignment of consciousness and relational harmony is the sole lawful outcome.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process wherein violating party acknowledges breach and assumes full responsibility for energetic and relational disruption
Engage guardian-caretaker dyad in re-establishment protocol to restore trust and protective coherence
Facilitate consciousness reintegration through guided awareness practices affirming relational dharma
Implement capacity restoration framework ensuring no repetition through structural and attitudinal alignment
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores relational integrity, upholds custodial dharma, and affirms that true justice is the realignment of consciousness—not infliction of suffering. Dharma is now restored.
